issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: 'Survival guilt' is hard to reconcile with a stalking trauma in the absence of any indication that other people died or were put at comparable lethal risk. For this trauma type, that appraisal is clinically implausible rather than merely unusual.

issues.item: Triggers: Gustatory (Taste): A specific taste associated with the event
issues.explanation: A specific taste trigger is not impossible, but for stalking it lacks support from the rest of the profile: there are no memory items or contextual details suggesting an event involving gustatory cues. Given the formulation also has no Triggers ↔ Memory linkage, this trigger is clinically unsupported and difficult to explain in this profile.

vignette:
Mark was a 32-year-old man who had always prided himself on his ability to connect with others, whether through his work as a tutor or in his personal life. He was married to Sarah, a kind and understanding woman who had supported him through thick and thin. However, since the traumatic events that had unfolded over the last year, Mark found himself retreating into a shell, his vibrant spirit dimmed by a weight he could not shake.

The stalking began when Mark noticed an unfamiliar figure lingering outside the café where he often met his students. At first, he brushed it off as paranoia, but the sense of being followed grew stronger. He now recognized that the man had been watching him for days, perhaps even weeks. The feeling of being hunted became inescapable; shadows morphed into threats, and every motorcycle roar felt like an ominous reminder of the figure in the café. The sound of a revving engine sent shivers down his spine, twisting his gut into knots, as he recalled the adrenaline-fueled moments of being acutely aware of the eyes on him. 

Mark’s life shifted dramatically after that. He began avoiding unfamiliar places altogether, convinced that danger lurked just beyond the familiar corners of his life. He would cancel tutoring sessions that required him to meet in new environments, opting instead for the safety of his home or well-trodden locales. Each day, he would tell himself that he was being sensible, yet deep down, he feared that he was only reinforcing his isolation. His students began to notice his reluctance to explore new ideas or experiences, and Mark felt their disappointment keenly, but he couldn’t shake the conviction that he was doing the right thing.

At home, intimacy with Sarah became a distant memory. The emotional closeness that once defined their relationship now felt like a perilous venture. Mark avoided conversations that could lead to deeper connections, fearing that any vulnerability might expose him to more pain. He felt undeserving of her affection and even began to punish himself for not being the husband she deserved. “I brought this upon myself,” he would think, as he scrolled through messages from friends, ignoring their invitations and support. Every moment of joy seemed tainted by his belief that he was responsible for the turmoil that had invaded his life.

Sleep became a luxury he could no longer afford. Mark lay awake at night, tossing and turning, haunted by the fear that he might wake to the sight of that lurking figure. The darkness became a breeding ground for his anxious thoughts, and he would often startle at the slightest noise, convinced that danger was imminent. Even mundane sounds, like the creaking of their old house or the hum of a passing car, felt like alarming signals, triggering a cascade of panic. He had started to avoid relaxation practices altogether, thinking it was safer to remain tense and vigilant.

As time went on, Mark's self-doubt grew. He found himself questioning his instincts and decisions, wondering if he could ever navigate the world without being ensnared by a sense of impending doom. Distrust seeped into his interactions, casting a shadow over his relationships. He no longer believed that people were genuinely kind; he thought they were hiding their true intentions. The paranoia was suffocating, and with every encounter, he felt a familiar tightening in his chest, as if he were still being stalked, even in the company of friends.

One evening, after a particularly restless night, Mark broke down in tears, overwhelmed by the realization that the life he used to cherish had slipped through his fingers. Sarah, seeing the depth of his pain, gently urged him to seek help. It was a turning point for Mark; he recognized that he could no longer carry this burden alone. He was terrified of confronting his demons but also hopeful that perhaps, with support, he could reclaim a part of himself that had been lost.

Sitting in the therapist's office, Mark felt a mix of fear and anticipation. He had come to understand that healing would not be easy, but he longed for the chance to trust again, to feel safe in his own skin, and to reconnect with Sarah on a deeper level. What frightened him most was the possibility that he might never fully escape the grip of his experiences, yet the flicker of hope urged him to take the first step toward a life unbound by fear.
